cases.name: memory_is_one_untrusted_user_message
cases.rule: Injected memory is exactly one user message, marked untrusted, carrying the watermark and the plan; never system, never assistant.

cases.name: recall_failure_is_not_fatal
cases.rule: When recall is unavailable the agent runs without memory: no memory message, no error raised to the turn, and the turn is still stored.

cases.name: write_failure_is_never_silent
cases.rule: When the store is unavailable the failure is surfaced to the application; a lost turn is invisible until a subject access request asks for it.

turn.user: Remember that I prefer written notes.

cases.name: store_only_on_success
cases.rule: A failed turn is not a memory: when the model call fails nothing is observed.

turn.user: Remember that I prefer written notes.

cases.name: filters_default_to_external_messages
cases.rule: Internal tool traffic does not become memory by default: only the person's message and the final reply are observed. Each observed message stands alone: what was not one atomic unit in the turn is not one in the memory.

turn.assistant: Room A is booked for Tuesday.

cases.name: no_synthetic_message_reaches_observe
cases.rule: A message the framework wrote, a summary or the injected memory itself, is never observed as though a person said it.

synthetic.content: Summary of earlier conversation: the user asked about colleagues.

cases.name: compaction_hands_the_model_the_deployments_context
cases.rule: When compaction is due the adapter asks the deployment for the subject's context and hands the model exactly that: one untrusted user message with the segments and the verbatim turns unchanged, in place of the history the framework held. The person's message stays; nothing synthetic is observed.

cases.name: context_failure_is_not_fatal
cases.rule: When the context cannot be fetched the history stays as the framework held it: no memory message, no error raised to the turn, and the turn is still stored.

cases.name: a_retried_turn_is_stored_once
cases.rule: A turn the application retries is one memory: the adapter derives the observation's idempotency key from the turn itself, so the retry carries the same key and the deployment folds it into the observation it already holds.

turn.user: I moved to Oslo last month.

cases.name: a_turn_retried_a_second_later_is_stored_once
cases.rule: A retry that comes a second or more after the first attempt, as one after a timeout does, is still one memory. An adapter may stamp the time it stores a turn; the deployment recognises the same turn under the same key whatever time the retry carries.
